doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Frankie Valli's 'Swearin' to God' and drummer Gordon Edwards
summary: The Valli session, and Gordon Edwards' natural groove without strong reading.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah. Not particularly that record but I remember I did “Swearin’ to God” with Frankie Valli and I’m playing on “Swearin’ to God.” That was with a big band. And I felt like that was — something was happening there you know. I really felt like it. Because actually he tracked. He sang with us but he didn’t record. He sang in a booth while we recorded, which was a rehearsal for him also. And I remember it just had a groove happening. And there was a bass player on it, I forget who it was, Elliot Randall was on that. Remember Elliot Randall? Guitar player? He’s on that. There was a percussionist, he’s no longer with us. But this bass player, he was the bass player that you played with

that no matter what kind of music it was it felt great man. It could be a polka man. It could be a stupid — he just had a way of playing that you just knew that it was right. Like this guy just knows. And he was just a guy that did gigs around town you know, big black guy, nicest guy in the world. What the hell is his name? Gordon?
You got it. Gordon Edwards that’s right, that’s right.

Oh man, how about that guy? And not a lot of chops. And another thing about him was he would be on a jingle or something. And a lot of jingle writers, they write out everything. And he was a natural player. And he — of course you don’t ever want to give the impression that you don’t know how to read you know in a situation like that. And Gordon would look at the part, “Oh yeah, yeah man, oh yeah.” I mean he’d act like he was reading but he couldn’t read that much. But he played the shit out of it. He played the shit out of the music, not the notes. “It’s not the notes,” my brother used to say, “it’s the music.” It’s not the notes, you don’t play the notes, you play the music. The difference between a great player and a mediocre. It’s the music. Some of those guys, I wonder what happened to Gordon. I lost track of a lot of people man, when the business changed you know we don’t see each other that much. We used to see each other on dates you know.
